plan.topic: 'Mounjaro and Zepbound recall' headlines vs what the FDA enforcement report actually lists: a Class II recall (classified Oct 8, 2026) of 22 multi-dose vials of compounded tirzepatide for lack of assurance of sterility
plan.angle: Title: 'Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Actually Listed #shorts'. Answer by 10 s: 'Per the FDA Enforcement Report, a Class II recall classified [exact FDA date], 2026 covers 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide from Apothecary Pharma, not branded pens [only if confirmed on publish day].' One line: compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved, and anything injected has to be sterile. One line on what Class II means, in FDA wording. Action: check the FDA recall listings and ask your pharmacist or prescriber. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Prescriber line. 170 words or fewer. No sellers, no sourcing, no emoji, no #Mounjaro or #Zepbound.
plan.working_title: Mounjaro or Zepbound Recalled? What the FDA Actually Listed #shorts
plan.why: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' is our strongest Short lane (median 108). Oct 20 headlines tied brand names to a compounded recall, which causes search confusion we can calmly correct with a new FDA fact. | fact-check: The core record checks out in coverage of the FDA enforcement report: Apothecary Pharma LLC (Cary, NC) voluntarily recalled 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide (18 mg/mL, 4 mL multidose vials) for lack of assurance of sterility, and it was classified Class II. Three problems: (1) Date. Secondary sources give the classification as Oct 10, 2026, not Oct 8 (the recall began Sept 24). Take the date from the FDA Enforcement Report entry itself and use exactly that. (2) It isn't the only one. Houston RX recalled 64 vials of compounded tirzepatide-niacinamide (Class II, sterility, started Sept 25), and Carolina Infusion is also mentioned. Our 10-20 S1 seems to have used '64 vials', so this may repeat yesterday's topic. To pass the variety guard, the piece must add a new fact: the 22-vial Apothecary listing and the 'branded-name headline vs compounded record' point. It must not re-tell Houston RX. Don't say 'the recall' as if there were only one. Say 'recent FDA-listed recalls of compounded tirzepatide'. (3) Title: putting Mounjaro and Zepbound first, on a compounded recall, makes it look like the branded drugs were recalled, and our craft rules ban brand tags on compounded-recall posts. Only say 'no branded Mounjaro or Zepbound pens were listed' if a search of the FDA Enforcement Report on publish day confirms it, credited and dated. Give the Class II definition in FDA wording. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved or reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality. No emoji, no brand hashtags.

social.instagram_caption:
That "Mounjaro recall" headline? The FDA report lists compounded tirzepatide vials, not Lilly's branded Mounjaro or Zepbound. Here's what it actually says.

The FDA Enforcement Report lists a Class II recall, classified October 8, 2026, for 22 multi-dose vials of compounded tirzepatide from one compounder.

The listed reason: lack of assurance of sterility. That means sterility couldn't be assured, not that contamination was confirmed. Compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved, so the FDA doesn't verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they're marketed.

Class II means, in the FDA's words, use "may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences," or the probability of serious ones is remote.

Save this as a reminder to check the FDA's own recall listings before trusting a headline, and talk to your pharmacist or prescriber with questions. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against FDA primary records, and they're accurate. openFDA recall D-0036-2027 shows Apothecary Pharma LLC's "Tirzepatide Injection, 18mg/mL, 4 mL Sterile Multi-Dose Vial". It lists 22 vials, Class II, the FDA classified it on 2026-10-08, it appeared in the 2026-10-14 Enforcement Report, the reason is "Lack of Assurance of Sterility", and its status is ongoing. That supports s2. The "several recent" line in s3 holds up too: the same report has five more compounded tirzepatide recalls from Carolina Infusion (Class II, all sterility-related), and New Life Pharma had two in March 2026. The Class II quote in s5 matches the FDA definitions page word for word. The line in s4 about compounded drugs not being FDA-approved matches FDA's Compounding Q&A, which uses the word "verify". The framing is calm, the hook is answered by about 10 s, no seller is promoted, and the prescriber line and the "don't stop or change your medicines on your own" line are both there. A few small fixes remain: src1 points to the general Enforcement Reports index page instead of the recall record, src2 has the wrong year, one wording tweak in s4, and the "pens" wording in s3.

issues.claim: "the FDA doesn't review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they're marketed"
issues.problem: FDA's exact verb is "verify". Our rules say to keep the source's exact verb.
issues.fix: Narration: "And compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved, so the FDA doesn't verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they're marketed." List item: "FDA doesn't verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before marketing"

issues.claim: "The listed reason: lack of assurance of sterility."
issues.problem: It's accurate, but a viewer could read it as contamination having been found. The listing says sterility couldn't be assured, not that contamination was found. One clarifying sentence would keep the calm 'what's confirmed?' frame.
issues.fix: After the first sentence, add: "That means sterility couldn't be assured, not that contamination was confirmed." (Keep the Short at 170 words or fewer; it's about 150 now.)

issues.claim: "not branded Mounjaro or Zepbound pens" / "Compounded, not branded pens"
issues.problem: Branded Zepbound also comes in single-dose vials, so 'pens' alone could leave someone with a branded vial unsure whether theirs is affected. Naming the maker is clearer.
issues.fix: Narration: "That's compounded tirzepatide, not Lilly's branded Mounjaro or Zepbound." on_screen_text: "Compounded, not Lilly's branded"

issues.problem: The prescriber line is there, but the 'not personal advice' disclaimer isn't spoken or shown, and this is a recall/safety piece.
issues.fix: Narration: "Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you. Follow for more." on_screen_text: "Not personal advice. Ask your prescriber"

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at -13.5dB under voice (right in the -12/-15 window) and swells to -10.4dB in pauses, about 3.5dB hotter than the -14dB pause target, so I pulled the whole bed down ~1.5dB (0.85x) rather than touching per-cue ducking, which keeps speech-under level fine while taming pause swells. SFX: thinned four redundant simultaneous duplicates (10,14,24,39,59 — paired identical whoosh/bubble/tick hits that add nothing) and cut the 58.18-59.63s cluster from 7 cues down to 4 (43,45,47,49) to respect the 3-4/second ceiling. Pulled down the two effects riding over the "Sterility: not assured" dramatic line (25,26) and the ding/pop that poked above -14dB during speech (6,43) so nothing crowds the narrator. Added three bespoke, low-key custom SFX (opening clinical beep, a single ominous heartbeat-thud under the sterility line, and a soft regulatory stamp under "Not FDA-approved") to give the key beats texture without adding clutter.
